page.layout: One column of text on the page, with the printed page number top right and the running head "LATINA." top centre. No marginal notes. The signature "c 3" stands at the foot below the last line.

main_text.p: tivo. Comparativus autem, addito or, pro communi genere, & us, pro neutro: ut, à Docti, gelehrt / Doctior, Doctius, à tenui, dünn / tenuior, tenuius, à felici, glückselig / felicior, felicius. Superlativus, addito issimus, pro masculino, issima pro foemino, issimum pro neutro: ut, doctissimus, doctissima, doctissimum. Si tamen positivus desinat in er, superlativus masculinus fit, addito rimus, foemininus addito rima, neuter rimum: ut niger, schwarz / nigerrimus, nigerrima, nigerrimum. Quidam positivi formant Superlativos in limus: ut facilis, leicht / facilimus. Agilis, schnel und fertig / agilimus. Gracilis, dünn und mager / gracilimus. Humilis, niederträchtig und demütig / humilimus. Similis, gleich / similimus.
main_text.l: Bonus, gut / melior, besser / optimus, der beste.
Malus, böß / pejor, erger / pessimus, der ergste.
Magnus, groß / major, größer / maximus, der größte.
Parvus, klein / minor, kleiner / minimus, der kleinste. Et parvissimus, Lucretio.
Multum, viel / plus, mehr / plurimum, das meiste.
Vetus, alt / veterior, elter / veterrimus, der elteste.
Pius, Gottsfürchtig / magis pius, maxime pius.
main_text.p: Piissimus apud Diomedem, Senecam & Cuttium reperitur: Et apud quosdam alios pientissimus.
Reliqua omnia, vocalem ante us vel is habentia per magis & maxime describuntur: praeter tenuis, tenuior, & strenuus, strenuior.
main_text.l: Dexter, recht / oder glückhafftig / dexterior, dextimus.
Maturus, zeitig oder reiffe / maturior, maturrimus & maturissimus.

page.notes: The asterisk-like mark beside "strenuus" in the right margin is a stray printer's mark, not a note, so it is left out. The symbol before "ottsfürchtig" is a printed sign, not a letter; it is left out and the German word is kept. "Superlativus" forms of "issimus" appear with a long-s-like letter in print and are written as plain s. The German glosses are in black letter and marked bl. Some German words are at the edge of legibility, notably "gelehrt", "glückselig" and "erger"; they are copied as seen and may be off. The printed "maturrimus" is left as printed.
